page: Microsoft Azure E8-2ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for workloads that require high memory allocations with constrained vCPU counts. Powered by the AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance exposes 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The CPU incorporates 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside core extensions including AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

Hardware provisioning delivers 64.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a notable ratio of 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance is not equipped with discrete GPUs. Bundled local ephemeral storage consists of a 322 GB SSD, providing high-speed scratch space directly attached to the host. Networking configurations do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements reflect the asymmetric hardware ratio. Single-core performance demonstrates solid results, registering 2,696.08 in stress-ng single-core tests (top 25%) and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,580.0. However, because overall compute is limited to 2 vCPUs, multi-core metrics rank low, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 1,972.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 3,136.94. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 31.81 GB/sec, while write bandwidth tests at 22.36 GB/sec. Application testing records Redis SET operations at 2.04 million operations per second and static web throughput of 2.58 GB/sec.

The constrained core configuration combined with a 64 GB memory capacity makes Microsoft Azure E8-2ads_v5 cost-effective for memory-heavy software licensed per core. Typical target workloads include relational databases with per-core licensing constraints, in-memory caching layers, medium-scale ETL processing, and analytics jobs requiring extensive working memory without substantial parallel execution demands.
